`abstract class Node`<br/>
**Implements:** [`INode`](/reference/nodes/inode/)<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`ChartNode`](/reference/nodes/chartnode/), [`RadarChartNode`](/reference/nodes/radarchartnode/), [`BaseCheckboxNode`](/reference/controls/basecheckboxnode/), [`BaseChoiceNode`](/reference/controls/basechoicenode/), [`FieldNode`](/reference/controls/fieldnode/), [`BaseScrollbarNode`](/reference/controls/basescrollbarnode/), [`BaseToggleNode`](/reference/controls/basetogglenode/), [`DevNode`](/reference/nodes/devnode/), [`ContainerNode`](/reference/layout/containernode/), [`FlexNode`](/reference/layout/flexnode/), [`GridNode`](/reference/layout/gridnode/), [`BaseModelNode`](/reference/nodes/basemodelnode/), [`ProgressNode`](/reference/nodes/progressnode/), [`ResourceNode`](/reference/nodes/resourcenode/), [`ResourcePlayerNode`](/reference/nodes/resourceplayernode/), [`CircleNode`](/reference/nodes/circlenode/), [`RectNode`](/reference/nodes/rectnode/), [`TextNode`](/reference/nodes/textnode/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.ui.node` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [Node.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/ui/node/Node.java)

Base class of every element of a UI, a box in design pixels with children, fluent properties, input, hover, scroll, drag and effects.

## Description

Every shape, text, image, control and container of a UI extends `Node`.
You use it through its subclasses: create a node with the factory of its class, chain its setters, build its children in `body(...)`, react with `onX(...)` listeners, and end the chain with `attach(...)`:

```java file="com/example/reference/CardUI.java" region="node"
```

A node is placed relative to its parent, in design pixels; its children are drawn over it in the order of their `zindex` and receive the input before it.
Most setters also take a `Supplier` or a signal, so that the property follows a value that changes.
To draw a node of your own, extend a node class and override the hooks of [`INode`](/reference/nodes/inode/).
JOID calls every hook and every listener of a node on the render thread.

<a id="Node-events"></a>

## Events

### Lifecycle

| Event | Listener | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [onUpdate](#Node-event-onUpdate) | [`EventListener<NodeEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodeevent/) | Adds a listener that runs on every frame, after the children and the `update` hook. |
| [onDetach](#Node-event-onDetach) | [`EventListener<NodeEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodeevent/) | Adds a listener that runs when the node leaves its UI, after its children and its own `detach`. |
| [onInit](#Node-event-onInit) | [`EventListener<NodeEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodeevent/) | Adds a listener that runs when the node is loaded into a UI, after `init`. |
| [onRender](#Node-event-onRender) | [`EventListener<NodeDrawEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodedrawevent/) | Adds a listener that runs at the end of the drawing of the node, after its children and its layers. |
| [onDraw](#Node-event-onDraw) | [`EventListener<NodeDrawEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodedrawevent/) | Adds a listener that runs after the node has drawn itself, before its label and its children in front. |
| [onMount](#Node-event-onMount) | [`EventListener<NodeEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodeevent/) | Adds a listener that runs on each frame where the node becomes mounted: the first frame where it is drawn mounted, then again after a detach or after a `wait` condition stopped holding. |

### Hover and tooltips

| Event | Listener | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [onHoverStart](#Node-event-onHoverStart) | [`EventListener<NodeHoverEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodehoverevent/) | Adds a listener that runs when the mouse enters the node. |
| [onHover](#Node-event-onHover) | [`EventListener<NodeHoverEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodehoverevent/) | Adds a listener that runs on every frame while the node is hovered. |
| [onHoverEnd](#Node-event-onHoverEnd) | [`EventListener<NodeHoverEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodehoverevent/) | Adds a listener that runs when the mouse leaves the node, or when the node is hidden or detached while hovered. |

### Scrolling

| Event | Listener | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [onScroll](#Node-event-onScroll) | [`EventListener<NodeScrollEvent.Post<T>>`](/reference/events/nodescrollevent-post/) | Adds a listener that runs after the scroll has changed. |
| [onScrollToEnd](#Node-event-onScrollToEnd) | [`EventListener<NodeScrollEvent.Post<T>>`](/reference/events/nodescrollevent-post/) | Adds a listener that runs when a scroll heads for the end of the content, before the content gets there: the moment to load more. |
| [onScrollEndReached](#Node-event-onScrollEndReached) | [`EventListener<NodeScrollEvent.Post<T>>`](/reference/events/nodescrollevent-post/) | Adds a listener that runs when the shown content has reached the end after a scroll toward it. |

### Drag and drop

| Event | Listener | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [onDragStart](#Node-event-onDragStart) | [`EventListener<NodeDragEvent.Post<T>>`](/reference/events/nodedragevent-post/) | Adds a listener that runs once a drag has started. |
| [onDrag](#Node-event-onDrag) | [`EventListener<NodeDragEvent.Post<T>>`](/reference/events/nodedragevent-post/) | Adds a listener that runs at every mouse move of the drag. |
| [onDragDrop](#Node-event-onDragDrop) | [`EventListener<NodeDragEvent.Post<T>>`](/reference/events/nodedragevent-post/) | Adds a listener that runs once the node has been dropped; the event holds the snap target, or `null`. |
| [onDragSnap](#Node-event-onDragSnap) | [`EventListener<NodeDragEvent.Post<T>>`](/reference/events/nodedragevent-post/) | Adds a listener that runs when the node is dropped on one of its snap targets, after `onDragDrop`. |

### Other events

| Event | Listener | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [onMove](#Node-event-onMove) | [`EventListener<NodeChangeEvent.Post<T,Point>>`](/reference/events/nodechangeevent-post/) | Adds a listener that runs after the node has moved. |
| [onChildAppend](#Node-event-onChildAppend) | [`EventListener<NodeChildEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodechildevent/) | Adds a listener that runs when a child is added to the node; moving an existing child to the front does not fire it. |
| [onClick](#Node-event-onClick) | [`EventListener<NodeMouseEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodemouseevent/) | Adds a listener that runs when the left button is pressed on the hovered node, unless a node in front consumed the press; the press is then consumed. |
| [onAnimate](#Node-event-onAnimate) | [`EventListener<NodeAnimateEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodeanimateevent/) | Adds a listener that runs when the value of a followed animator changes, during the update of the node. |
| [onWatch](#Node-event-onWatch) | [`EventListener<NodeWatchEvent<T>>`](/reference/events/nodewatchevent/) | Adds a listener that runs after a `watch` of the node has applied its properties. |

## Creation details

<a id="Node-constructor"></a>

### Node

`Node(double x, double y)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Creates a node at `x`, `y` with a size of `0`, for a subclass whose size comes from its content.

`Node(double x, double y, double width, double height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Creates a node at `x`, `y` with this width and height, in design pixels.
A subclass calls it from its own constructor; [`Node.copy`](/reference/nodes/node/#Node-method-copy) calls a constructor with these four arguments.

## Property details

<a id="Node-property-x"></a>

### x

- `this x(double x)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this x(Signal<Double> x)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this x(Supplier<Double> x)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `double getX()` 

**Default:** 

Horizontal position of the anchor point of the node, in design pixels, from the left edge of its parent (or of the canvas for a root or `ABSOLUTE` node).
A writable signal is bound both ways: a drag or `move` writes the new position to it; a lambda or a read-only signal cannot be combined with a `MOVE` drag and throws an `IllegalStateException`.

<a id="Node-property-y"></a>

### y

- `this y(double y)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this y(Signal<Double> y)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this y(Supplier<Double> y)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `double getY()` 

**Default:** 

Vertical position of the anchor point of the node, in design pixels, from the top edge of its parent (or of the canvas for a root or `ABSOLUTE` node).
It binds to a signal like `x`.

<a id="Node-property-width"></a>

### width

- `this width(double width)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this width(Supplier<Double> width)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `double getWidth()` 

**Default:** 

Width of the node, in design pixels.
`0` lets a node that measures its content (text, image, flex, grid) take the width of its content.

<a id="Node-property-height"></a>

### height

- `this height(double height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this height(Supplier<Double> height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `double getHeight()` 

**Default:** 

Height of the node, in design pixels.
`0` lets a node that measures its content take the height of its content.

<a id="Node-property-position"></a>

### position

- `this position(PositionProperty position)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this position(Supplier<PositionProperty> position)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `PositionProperty getPosition()` 

**Default:** `PositionProperty.RELATIVE`

`RELATIVE` places the node inside its parent; `ABSOLUTE` places it on the canvas whatever its parents, out of their layout, their scroll and their content size.

<a id="Node-property-anchor"></a>

### anchor

- `this anchor(Align anchor)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this anchor(Supplier<Align> anchor)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>

**Default:** 

Sets `anchorX` and `anchorY` to the same value.

<a id="Node-property-anchorX"></a>

### anchorX

- `this anchorX(Align anchorX)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this anchorX(Supplier<Align> anchorX)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `Align getAnchorX()` 

**Default:** `Align.START`

Which point of the node sits at `x` and stays in place when the width changes: `START` the left edge, `CENTER` the middle, `END` the right edge.

<a id="Node-property-anchorY"></a>

### anchorY

- `this anchorY(Align anchorY)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this anchorY(Supplier<Align> anchorY)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `Align getAnchorY()` 

**Default:** `Align.START`

Which point of the node sits at `y` and stays in place when the height changes: `START` the top edge, `CENTER` the middle, `END` the bottom edge.

<a id="Node-property-aspectRatio"></a>

### aspectRatio

- `this aspectRatio(double aspectRatio)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this aspectRatio(Supplier<Double> aspectRatio)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `double getAspectRatio()` 

**Default:** none, the width and the height stay free

Width divided by height that the node keeps on every frame: JOID computes the height from the width, or the width from the height when the width is `0`.
A value of `0` or below turns it off.

<a id="Node-property-zindex"></a>

### zindex

- `this zindex(int zindex)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this zindex(Supplier<Integer> zindex)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `int getZindex()` 

**Default:** 

Order of the node among its siblings: a higher value is drawn above and receives the input first.
A negative value draws the child behind its parent.

<a id="Node-property-zlevel"></a>

### zlevel

- `this zlevel(double zlevel)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this zlevel(Supplier<Double> zlevel)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `double getZlevel()` 

**Default:** 

Depth of the node along the Z axis, added to the depth of its parent.

<a id="Node-property-skeleton"></a>

### skeleton

- `this skeleton(Function<T,Node> skeleton)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `Node getSkeleton()` 

**Default:** 

Placeholder node drawn instead of this node and its children while one of its `wait` conditions fails; the function receives the node and returns the placeholder, or `null` for the default skeleton.

<a id="Node-property-visible"></a>

### visible

- `this visible(boolean visible)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this visible(Supplier<Boolean> visible)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `boolean isVisible()` 

**Default:** `true`

If `false`, the node and its children are neither drawn nor sent any input, and a layout node leaves them out.

<a id="Node-property-enabled"></a>

### enabled

- `this enabled(boolean enabled)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this enabled(Supplier<Boolean> enabled)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `boolean isEnabled()` 

**Default:** `true`

If `false`, the node and its children are drawn but ignore the input and show no hover progress.

<a id="Node-property-interactive"></a>

### interactive

- `this interactive(boolean interactive)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this interactive(Supplier<Boolean> interactive)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `boolean isInteractive()` 

**Default:** `true`

If `false`, the node and its children let the mouse through to what is under them and are never hovered.

<a id="Node-property-cursor"></a>

### cursor

- `this cursor(Cursor cursor)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this cursor(Supplier<Cursor> cursor)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `Cursor getCursor()` 

**Default:** 

Cursor shown while the mouse is over the node; `null` uses the cursor of the closest parent that has one.

<a id="Node-property-hoverDuration"></a>

### hoverDuration

- `this hoverDuration(long hoverDuration)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this hoverDuration(Supplier<Long> hoverDuration)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `long getHoverDuration()` 

**Default:** `200L`

Time, in ms, that the hover progress takes to go from `0` to `1` and back.

<a id="Node-property-hoverEquation"></a>

### hoverEquation

- `this hoverEquation(TweenEquation hoverEquation)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this hoverEquation(Supplier<TweenEquation> hoverEquation)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `TweenEquation getHoverEquation()` 

**Default:** `TweenEquations.LINEAR`

Easing of the hover progress.

<a id="Node-property-hover"></a>

### hover

- `this hover(IHoverElement element)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this hover(HoverSupplier supplier)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this hover(Supplier<List<String>> supplier)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>

**Default:** 

Adds a tooltip shown while the node is hovered: a [`IHoverElement`](/reference/nodes/ihoverelement/), a [`HoverSupplier`](/reference/nodes/hoversupplier/) that gives one line (`null` for none), or a `Supplier` of lines drawn by [`UI.drawHover`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-drawHover).
Each call adds one more element.

<a id="Node-property-overflow"></a>

### overflow

- `this overflow(OverflowProperty overflow)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this overflow(Supplier<OverflowProperty> overflow)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `OverflowProperty getOverflow()` 

**Default:** `OverflowProperty.NONE`

What the node does with children that go past its bounds: `NONE` draws them, `HIDDEN` clips them, `SCROLL` clips them and lets the wheel scroll them.

<a id="Node-property-scrollSpeed"></a>

### scrollSpeed

- `this scrollSpeed(double scrollSpeed)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this scrollSpeed(Supplier<Double> scrollSpeed)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `double getScrollSpeed()` 

**Default:** `1D`

Factor applied to the wheel: one notch scrolls 30 design pixels times this factor, twice as far with Control down.

<a id="Node-property-scrollbar"></a>

### scrollbar

- `this scrollbar(BaseScrollbarNode scrollbar)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `BaseScrollbarNode getScrollbar()` 

**Default:** 

Scrollbar that scrolls this node; it is drawn when the overflow is `SCROLL` and the content goes past the node.

<a id="Node-property-label"></a>

### label

- `this label(Text label)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this label(Supplier<Text> label)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `Text getLabel()` 

**Default:** 

Text drawn centered over the node, after the node itself and before its children; `null` draws none.

<a id="Node-property-draggable"></a>

### draggable

- `this draggable(DraggableProperty draggable)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this draggable(Supplier<DraggableProperty> draggable)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `DraggableProperty getDraggable()` 

**Default:** 

Lets the user drag the node with the left button, inside the area and with the movement and the snapping of the [`DraggableProperty`](/reference/nodes/draggableproperty/); `null` means the node cannot be dragged.

## Method details

<a id="Node-method-load"></a>

### load

`void load(UI ui)` 

Attaches the node to the UI: loads its children, its scrollbar, its skeleton and its effects, runs `init` and fires `onInit`.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` when a required part or setting is missing; JOID calls it for you when the node joins an open UI.

<a id="Node-method-render"></a>

### render

`void render(double mouseX, double mouseY)` 

Draws the node for this frame: applies its layout, its hover and its scroll, then draws its children behind it, itself, its label, its children in front and its layers, through its effects.
Its parent or its UI calls it; you never call it.

<a id="Node-method-renderHover"></a>

### renderHover

`boolean renderHover(double mouseX, double mouseY)` 

Draws the tooltips of the node at the mouse and returns `true` when it has one.
The UI calls it on the hovered node, then on its parents until one draws.

<a id="Node-method-updateScroll"></a>

### updateScroll

`this updateScroll()` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Moves the shown scroll to its target at once, on both axes, without the smooth movement.

<a id="Node-method-updateScrollX"></a>

### updateScrollX

`this updateScrollX()` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Moves the shown horizontal scroll to its target at once.

<a id="Node-method-updateScrollY"></a>

### updateScrollY

`this updateScrollY()` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Moves the shown vertical scroll to its target at once.

<a id="Node-method-append"></a>

### append

`this append(Node... nodes)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds children to the node, in front of their siblings of the same `zindex`.
A node that has another parent or that is a root of a UI leaves it first; a child of this node moves to the front without being loaded again.
The children are loaded at once when the node is attached, and when it joins a UI otherwise; `onChildAppend` fires for each new child.

<a id="Node-method-attach"></a>

### attach

`this attach(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Attaches the node at the root of the UI, as [`UI.add`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-add) does.

`this attach(Node node)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds the node to the children of this parent, as [`Node.append`](/reference/nodes/node/#Node-method-append) does.

<a id="Node-method-body"></a>

### body

`this body(Runnable runnable)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Runs the code at once, to create the children where the node is created.

`this body(Consumer<T> consumer)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Runs the code at once with the node, to create its children; JOID keeps it to run it again when a `watch` rebuilds the node.

<a id="Node-method-handleMousePressed"></a>

### handleMousePressed

`this handleMousePressed(EventListener<NodeMouseEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that hears every mouse press of the UI, wherever the pointer is, after the children of the node in front and before its children behind; check `isHovered()` to react only over the node.
It does not run while the node is hidden, disabled or not interactive.
Consuming the event stops the nodes behind, the UI and the host; a `MONITOR` listener always hears it.

<a id="Node-method-handleMouseReleased"></a>

### handleMouseReleased

`this handleMouseReleased(EventListener<NodeMouseEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that hears a mouse release, wherever the mouse is.
It runs even on a hidden or disabled node, so that a gesture always ends.

<a id="Node-method-handleMouseDragged"></a>

### handleMouseDragged

`this handleMouseDragged(EventListener<NodeMouseEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that hears a mouse move while a button is held.
It does not run while the node is hidden, disabled or not interactive.

<a id="Node-method-handleMouseScroll"></a>

### handleMouseScroll

`this handleMouseScroll(EventListener<NodeMouseScrollEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that hears every wheel turn of the UI, wherever the pointer is, before the node scrolls; check `isHovered()` to react only over the node.
It does not run while the node is hidden, disabled or not interactive.

<a id="Node-method-handleCharTyped"></a>

### handleCharTyped

`this handleCharTyped(EventListener<NodeCharEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that hears a typed character, as a Unicode code point.
It does not run while the node is hidden or disabled, nor while it is scrolled out of view unless it holds the input.

<a id="Node-method-handleKeyPressed"></a>

### handleKeyPressed

`this handleKeyPressed(EventListener<NodeKeyEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that hears a key press.
It does not run while the node is hidden or disabled, nor while it is scrolled out of view unless it holds the input.

<a id="Node-method-handleKeyReleased"></a>

### handleKeyReleased

`this handleKeyReleased(EventListener<NodeKeyEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that hears a key release.
It runs even on a hidden or disabled node, so that a held key always ends.

<a id="Node-method-scrollX"></a>

### scrollX

`<T extends Node> T scrollX(double scrollX)` 

Sets the horizontal scroll, in design pixels: `0` shows the start, a negative value moves the content to the left.
The value is kept between the end of the content and `0`; a positive value warns once in dev mode.

`<T extends Node> T scrollX(Signal<Double> scrollX)` 

Binds the horizontal scroll to a signal: the node follows it, and a scroll by the user writes back to it.

<a id="Node-method-scrollY"></a>

### scrollY

`<T extends Node> T scrollY(double scrollY)` 

Sets the vertical scroll, in design pixels: `0` shows the top, a negative value moves the content up.
The value is kept between the end of the content and `0`; a positive value warns once in dev mode.

`<T extends Node> T scrollY(Signal<Double> scrollY)` 

Binds the vertical scroll to a signal, both ways.

### scrollTo

`this scrollTo(double x, double y)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

### remove

`this remove(Node... nodes)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Detaches these children from the node; a node that is not its child is ignored.

<a id="Node-method-self"></a>

### self

`this self(Consumer<T> consumer)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Runs the code at once with the node, to set it up without breaking the chain.

<a id="Node-method-copy"></a>

### copy

`<T extends Node> T copy()` 

Returns an unattached copy of the node and of its children, with their properties, listeners and effects.
A field that holds a node of the copied tree holds its copy; `transient` fields are left out.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` when the class has no constructor `(x, y, width, height)`, `(x, y)` or without argument and does not override `instantiate()`.

<a id="Node-method-useStore"></a>

### useStore

`this useStore(Class<T> clazz, Supplier<T> factory)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Returns the store of this class from the UI of the node, as [`UI.useStore`](/reference/ui/ui/#UI-method-useStore) does.

<a id="Node-method-addTask"></a>

### addTask

`this addTask(Task task)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Attaches a task to the node; it runs while the node belongs to an open UI.

<a id="Node-method-removeTask"></a>

### removeTask

`this removeTask(Task task)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Detaches a task from the node.

<a id="Node-method-addShortcut"></a>

### addShortcut

`this addShortcut(Shortcut shortcut)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Attaches a shortcut to the node; it fires while the node is visible and enabled.

<a id="Node-method-removeShortcut"></a>

### removeShortcut

`this removeShortcut(Shortcut shortcut)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Detaches a shortcut from the node.

<a id="Node-method-layoutPosition"></a>

### layoutPosition

`this layoutPosition(double layoutX, double layoutY)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Sets the offset that a layout adds to the declared position of the node.
A layout node or a control calls it on its children in `layout()`.

<a id="Node-method-layoutSize"></a>

### layoutSize

`this layoutSize(double width, double height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Sets the size of the node for this frame without changing its declared size.

<a id="Node-method-fit"></a>

### fit

`this fit(double contentWidth, double contentHeight)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Gives the node the size of its content on each axis whose declared size is `0`, and keeps the current size on the other.

<a id="Node-method-move"></a>

### move

`this move(double x, double y)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Moves the node to this declared position as a change: the `beforeMove` listeners can refuse it, bound signals are written, and a running drop animation stops there.

<a id="Node-method-beforeMove"></a>

### beforeMove

`this beforeMove(EventListener<NodeChangeEvent.Pre<T,Point>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs before the node moves, by a drag or `move`; cancelling the event keeps the node in place.

<a id="Node-method-hoverColor"></a>

### hoverColor

`Color hoverColor(Color color, Color hoveredColor)` 

The first color blended toward the second by the hover progress; a `null` second color returns the first.

<a id="Node-method-drawSkeleton"></a>

### drawSkeleton

`void drawSkeleton(double mouseX, double mouseY)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span>

Draws the default skeleton, a rectangle of the loading color on the bounds of the node.

<a id="Node-method-fireUpdate"></a>

### fireUpdate

`void fireUpdate()` 

Updates the node and its children for this frame: pulls its reactive values, runs `update` and fires `onUpdate`.
Its UI calls it once per frame; an `update` that throws prints a warning once.

<a id="Node-method-fireDetach"></a>

### fireDetach

`void fireDetach()` 

Detaches the node and its children from their UI: runs `detach`, ends the drag and the hover, detaches the effects and fires `onDetach`.

<a id="Node-method-fireMousePressed"></a>

### fireMousePressed

`boolean fireMousePressed(double mouseX, double mouseY, MouseButton button)` 

Sends a mouse press at this point to the node and its children, as the UI does, and returns `true` when something consumed it; use it to simulate an input.

`void fireMousePressed(double mouseX, double mouseY, MouseButton button, IConsumableEvent source)` 

Sends a mouse press that belongs to this source event: consuming it consumes the source.

<a id="Node-method-fireMouseReleased"></a>

### fireMouseReleased

`boolean fireMouseReleased(double mouseX, double mouseY, MouseButton button, long deltaTime)` 

Sends a mouse release of this button, pressed `deltaTime` ms before, to the node and its children and returns `true` when something consumed it.

`void fireMouseReleased(double mouseX, double mouseY, MouseButton button, long deltaTime, IConsumableEvent source)` 

Sends a mouse release that belongs to this source event.

<a id="Node-method-fireMouseDragged"></a>

### fireMouseDragged

`boolean fireMouseDragged(double mouseX, double mouseY, MouseButton button, long deltaTime)` 

Sends a mouse move with this button held for `deltaTime` ms and returns `true` when something consumed it.

`void fireMouseDragged(double mouseX, double mouseY, MouseButton button, long deltaTime, IConsumableEvent source)` 

Sends a mouse move that belongs to this source event.

<a id="Node-method-fireMouseScroll"></a>

### fireMouseScroll

`boolean fireMouseScroll(double mouseX, double mouseY, double notchesX, double notchesY)` 

Sends a wheel turn, in notches, and returns `true` when something consumed it.

`void fireMouseScroll(double mouseX, double mouseY, double notchesX, double notchesY, IConsumableEvent source)` 

Sends a wheel turn that belongs to this source event.

<a id="Node-method-fireCharTyped"></a>

### fireCharTyped

`boolean fireCharTyped(int codepoint)` 

Sends a typed character and returns `true` when something consumed it.

`void fireCharTyped(int codepoint, IConsumableEvent source)` 

Sends a typed character that belongs to this source event.

<a id="Node-method-fireKeyPressed"></a>

### fireKeyPressed

`boolean fireKeyPressed(Key physicalKey, Key key)` 

Sends a key press, its position on the keyboard then the key that the layout gives, and returns `true` when something consumed it.

`void fireKeyPressed(Key physicalKey, Key key, IConsumableEvent source)` 

Sends a key press that belongs to this source event.

<a id="Node-method-fireKeyReleased"></a>

### fireKeyReleased

`boolean fireKeyReleased(Key physicalKey, Key key)` 

Sends a key release and returns `true` when something consumed it.

`void fireKeyReleased(Key physicalKey, Key key, IConsumableEvent source)` 

Sends a key release that belongs to this source event.

<a id="Node-method-fireDragStart"></a>

### fireDragStart

`boolean fireDragStart(Runnable start)` 

Runs the `beforeDragStart` listeners, then the start and the `onDragStart` listeners unless a listener cancelled; returns `false` when it was cancelled.
A node that runs a drag of its own, such as a reorderable list, calls it.

<a id="Node-method-fireDrag"></a>

### fireDrag

`void fireDrag(Runnable drag)` 

Runs the move of the drag, then the `onDrag` listeners.

<a id="Node-method-fireDragDrop"></a>

### fireDragDrop

`boolean fireDragDrop(Node target, Runnable drop)` 

Runs the `beforeDragDrop` listeners, then the drop and the `onDragDrop` listeners unless a listener cancelled; returns `false` when it was cancelled.
`target` is the snap target, or `null`.

<a id="Node-method-listen"></a>

### listen

`<T extends Node> T listen(EventType<?> type, EventListener<?> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Adds a listener for an event type of the subclass; the `onX` methods of a node of your own call it.

<a id="Node-method-fire"></a>

### fire

`<E extends Event> E fire(EventType<? super E> type, Supplier<E> event)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Fires an event of the subclass to its listeners and returns it, or `null` when no listener exists, in which case the event is never built.

<a id="Node-method-start"></a>

### start

`<T extends Node, V> T start(String property, V value, Consumer<V> applier)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Sets a property to a plain value and applies it, replacing a previous `follow` or `bind` of the same property.

<a id="Node-method-follow"></a>

### follow

`<T extends Node, V> T follow(String property, Supplier<V> supplier, Consumer<V> applier)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Makes a property follow a `Supplier`: the applier receives each new value, when the signals it reads change or on every frame for a lambda.

<a id="Node-method-bind"></a>

### bind

`<T extends Node, V> T bind(String property, Signal<V> signal, Consumer<V> applier)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Binds a property to a signal: the applier receives each value of the signal.

`<T extends Node, V, M> T bind(String property, Signal<V> signal, Consumer<V> applier, Function<M,V> writer)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Binds a property to a signal both ways: `sync` writes the value back through the writer.

<a id="Node-method-bindNullable"></a>

### bindNullable

`<T extends Node, V, M> T bindNullable(String property, Signal<V> signal, Consumer<V> applier, Function<M,V> writer)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Binds a property to a signal both ways, accepting `null` values.

<a id="Node-method-sync"></a>

### sync

`void sync(String property, Object value)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Writes the value applied to a bound property back to its signal.

<a id="Node-method-require"></a>

### require

`<N extends Node> void require(String setting, String advice, Predicate<N> present)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: The … has no …, …

Declares a setting that the node needs: when the node loads without it, it throws an `IllegalStateException` that names the setting and gives the advice.

<a id="Node-method-part"></a>

### part

`<N extends Node> N part(Node previous, N next)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Replaces a part of the node, a child that the subclass places itself, by another one at the same place among the children, and returns it.

<a id="Node-method-reorderChildren"></a>

### reorderChildren

`void reorderChildren(List<Node> order)` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

Puts the children in this order, for drawing and for the layout.

<a id="Node-method-instantiate"></a>

### instantiate

`Node instantiate()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: The node … cannot be copied: its constructor … failed (…)
- `IllegalStateException`: The node … cannot be copied: declare a constructor (x, y, width, height) or override instantiate()

Creates the instance that `copy()` fills: it tries the constructors `(x, y, width, height)`, `(x, y)` and without argument.
Override it when the class has none of them.

<a id="Node-method-holdsInput"></a>

### holdsInput

`boolean holdsInput()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

If `true`, the node keeps receiving the input while it is scrolled out of the area of its container; `false` by default.
[`FieldNode`](/reference/controls/fieldnode/) holds it while it has the focus or a selection goes on, [`BaseSelectorNode`](/reference/controls/baseselectornode/) while it is open.

<a id="Node-method-isDraggingChild"></a>

### isDraggingChild

`boolean isDraggingChild(Node child)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

If `true`, the parent raises this child above its siblings because it is being dragged; a layout node that drags its children overrides it.

<a id="Node-method-getBindings"></a>

### getBindings

`NodeBindings getBindings()` <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

The reactive bindings of the node's properties, for a subclass.

## Event details

<a id="Node-event-onUpdate"></a>

### onUpdate

`this onUpdate(EventListener<NodeEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs on every frame, after the children and the `update` hook.

<a id="Node-event-onDetach"></a>

### onDetach

`this onDetach(EventListener<NodeEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when the node leaves its UI, after its children and its own `detach`.

<a id="Node-event-onInit"></a>

### onInit

`this onInit(EventListener<NodeEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when the node is loaded into a UI, after `init`.

<a id="Node-event-onRender"></a>

### onRender

`this onRender(EventListener<NodeDrawEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs at the end of the drawing of the node, after its children and its layers.

<a id="Node-event-onDraw"></a>

### onDraw

`this onDraw(EventListener<NodeDrawEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs after the node has drawn itself, before its label and its children in front.

<a id="Node-event-onMount"></a>

### onMount

`this onMount(EventListener<NodeEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs on each frame where the node becomes mounted: the first frame where it is drawn mounted, then again after a detach or after a `wait` condition stopped holding.

<a id="Node-event-onHoverStart"></a>

### onHoverStart

`this onHoverStart(EventListener<NodeHoverEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when the mouse enters the node.

<a id="Node-event-onHover"></a>

### onHover

`this onHover(EventListener<NodeHoverEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs on every frame while the node is hovered.

<a id="Node-event-onHoverEnd"></a>

### onHoverEnd

`this onHoverEnd(EventListener<NodeHoverEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when the mouse leaves the node, or when the node is hidden or detached while hovered.

<a id="Node-event-onScroll"></a>

### onScroll

`this onScroll(EventListener<NodeScrollEvent.Post<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs after the scroll has changed.

<a id="Node-event-onScrollToEnd"></a>

### onScrollToEnd

`this onScrollToEnd(EventListener<NodeScrollEvent.Post<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when a scroll heads for the end of the content, before the content gets there: the moment to load more.

<a id="Node-event-onScrollEndReached"></a>

### onScrollEndReached

`this onScrollEndReached(EventListener<NodeScrollEvent.Post<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when the shown content has reached the end after a scroll toward it.

<a id="Node-event-onDragStart"></a>

### onDragStart

`this onDragStart(EventListener<NodeDragEvent.Post<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs once a drag has started.

<a id="Node-event-onDrag"></a>

### onDrag

`this onDrag(EventListener<NodeDragEvent.Post<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs at every mouse move of the drag.

<a id="Node-event-onDragDrop"></a>

### onDragDrop

`this onDragDrop(EventListener<NodeDragEvent.Post<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs once the node has been dropped; the event holds the snap target, or `null`.

<a id="Node-event-onDragSnap"></a>

### onDragSnap

`this onDragSnap(EventListener<NodeDragEvent.Post<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when the node is dropped on one of its snap targets, after `onDragDrop`.

<a id="Node-event-onMove"></a>

### onMove

`this onMove(EventListener<NodeChangeEvent.Post<T,Point>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs after the node has moved.

<a id="Node-event-onChildAppend"></a>

### onChildAppend

`this onChildAppend(EventListener<NodeChildEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when a child is added to the node; moving an existing child to the front does not fire it.

<a id="Node-event-onClick"></a>

### onClick

`this onClick(EventListener<NodeMouseEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when the left button is pressed on the hovered node, unless a node in front consumed the press; the press is then consumed.

<a id="Node-event-onAnimate"></a>

### onAnimate

`this onAnimate(EventListener<NodeAnimateEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when the value of a followed animator changes, during the update of the node.

<a id="Node-event-onWatch"></a>

### onWatch

`this onWatch(EventListener<NodeWatchEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs after a `watch` of the node has applied its properties.

---

<small>`fluent` returns the instance, typed for chaining · `factory` creates an instance · `signal` also accepts a value that follows signals, as a signal, an expression or a lambda ([When does JOID compute this value again?](/use/learn/interactivity/signals/#ask-when-does-joid-compute-this-value-again)) · `hook` called by JOID, override it · `abstract` you implement it · `default` interface method with a body · `static` called on the class · `protected` visible to subclasses</small>
